summary: Gradual 5xx drift from prefetch queue growth causing intermittent circuit-trips in prod us-east
description: Issue summary: BrightWrite reported a steady rise in 5xx responses and degraded throughput beginning ~2026-03-10 02:00 UTC in us-east. Errors escalate slowly over several hours (5xx rate rising from ~0.2% to ~6%) and occasionally trigger api-gateway circuit-breaker marks against upstream serving clusters, resulting in short windows of routing to fallback variants. Impact: customer reports increased failed requests for embeddings and streaming generation, elevated tail latency, and intermittent session resets during business hours. Environment: prod (us-east), dedicated tenant BrightWrite. Observed timeline: 2026-03-10 01:45 UTC — first uptick in prefetch queue length on tenant shards. 2026-03-10 02:10 UTC — p95 prefetch latency increases from ~40ms to ~280ms; api-gateway 5xx begins to climb. 2026-03-10 04:20 UTC — gateway marks 2/6 upstream endpoints UNHEALTHY and triggers short circuit; traffic directed to fallbacks for ~30-90s. 2026-03-10 06:00 UTC — partial mitigation when prefetch-service recycle restored per-shard throughput. Steps to reproduce: 1) Run sustained small-batch embedding and short-chat generation mix targeting BrightWrite tenant with connection churn to emulate multiple clients. 2) Observe prefetch queue length and prefetch-service latency. 3) Track api-gateway health checks and circuit-breaker events. Logs/metrics: prefetch-service traces (grafana/dashboard/prefetch/tenant/BrightWrite), api-gateway health events (grafana/dashboard/apigw/health), runtime logs pointing to repeated kvcache shard lock attempts (logs.storage/kvcache/shard-47), support ticket timeline thread (#support-brightwrite on Slack).
comments: Support (2026-03-10 03:05) - Aisha Patel: Initial customer report received. Asked for request IDs and approximate time window. Customer provided sample request IDs and a short kinesis of errors.
Customer (BrightWrite) (2026-03-10 03:20) - Sara Liu: Confirmed failures across multiple users; attaching example request IDs: req_20260310_az1, req_20260310_bx9.
SRE (2026-03-10 04:00) - Miguel Torres: Noted correlated growth in prefetch queue size for BrightWrite shards; opened investigation into prefetch-service threadpool saturation.

SRE (2026-03-10 05:10) - Miguel Torres: Observed kvcache shard lock contention logs and a pattern of slow prefetch downstream acknowledgements. Temporarily increased prefetch concurrency for tenant to see effect.
Support (2026-03-10 06:30) - Aisha Patel: Communicated temporary mitigation to customer (restarted prefetch workers for tenant). Customer reports partial recovery; still seeing elevated p95.
Eng (2026-03-11 09:00) - Priya Desai: Deployed a canary that adds backoff jitter and reduces aggressive prefetch cancelation; monitoring for regressions.
Customer (2026-03-11 11:12) - Sara Liu: Noted much improved stability overnight; requests still show occasional 502s at peak times.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Prefetch-service queue growth per tenant causes blocking on kvcache shard locks, increasing request latency and causing api-gateway health checks to fail intermittently.
Hypothesis 2: Long-tail prefetch latency cascades into serving-runtime thread starvation under mixed workloads (embeddings + streaming) for dedicated tenants with pinned model instances.

Findings: p95 prefetch latency correlated strongly with increase in 5xx rate. kvcache logs show repeated lock retry backoffs on shard-47 and shard-53 belonging to BrightWrite. No NVML resets observed. Runtime GC pauses were normal range but thread pool utilization was at 92% during peak.
Experiment: Increased prefetch worker count for tenant and applied jitter to prefetch retry loop; this reduced immediate queue length but uncovered kvcache contention at the storage layer.
Related: prefetched keys show hot-key skew for a small set of prompt templates used by BrightWrite; suggests application-level access pattern causing kvcache hotspotting.
Linked prior incidents: SUP-214567 (backpressure propagation) contains similar kvcache contention notes but at cross-tenant scale.

Next investigative actions: capture flamegraphs from prefetch-service threads during the next peak window, enable per-shard lock telemetry for kvcache, and run a controlled load test that reproduces hot-key access patterns.
resolution: Workaround (2026-03-10): Recycled prefetch workers for BrightWrite tenant and temporarily increased prefetch concurrency to reduce queue buildup. This brought 5xx rate back toward baseline but did not eliminate spikes at peak.

Mitigation (2026-03-11): Deployed a canary patch to prefetch-service that adds randomized jitter to retry backoffs, caps per-tenant prefetch inflight, and adds backpressure metrics to Prometheus. Also scheduled a maintenance window to redistribute hot kvcache keys across shards.

Permanent next steps: 1) Implement adaptive per-tenant prefetch throttling driven by kvcache lock contention signals. 2) Add hotspot detection and automatic shard rebalancing for kvcache. 3) Update runbook to include explicit checks for prefetch queue growth as a leading indicator. 4) Follow up with BrightWrite on client-side prompt fanout patterns and recommend minor batching to reduce hot-key frequency.
Postmortem/Follow-up: Assign an action owner in SRE to track kvcache rebalancer RFC and schedule a cross-team review with Storage and Serving by 2026-03-25.
